 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 Oral Judgment

Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.1193/2012 dated 12.04.2018 passed by the Additional Court of Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge, Mysuru and Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Mysuru, the appellant/KSRTC is before this Court.
The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.4,48,874/- and interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

2. The facts of the case are that on 12.10.2011, the bus belonging to the corporation was moving on the side of the road slowly and in the meanwhile, another private bus came from the opposite side in a rash and negligent manner and also in a high speed and dashed the KSRTC bus.
Due to the impact of the accident, the bus of corporation was damaged and an amount of Rs.1,07,340/- was spent towards repairs.
The Tribunal by order impugned had granted compensation of an amount of Rs.1,07,340/-.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/KSRTC submits that the Tribunal had failed to grant the loss of revenue and also reduction value of the vehicle and on both counts, the compensation needs to be enhanced.
4.
Learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/ Insurance Company submits that to say that there is loss of revenue, no evidence is adduced.

It is submitted that in fact for an old vehicle, the Court had granted Rs.1,07,340/- for the repairs and there cannot be any diminishing of the value of the vehicle in fact it would have been enhanced.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.
First coming to the issue of loss of revenue, the appellant should have placed some material on record either before the Tribunal or before this Court.
No evidence is placed before the Court either with regard to the diminishing value of the vehicle or with regard to the loss of revenue.

On these grounds, the appeal Karnataka State Road vs Sri Shreekanta on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29726763/
2 of the Insurance Company has to fail.

entities.text: Karnataka State Road vs Sri Shreekanta
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that because the driver was not having a valid driving license, NC: 2025:KHC:15035 the Insurance Company is exonerated from the liability.
Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that no such ground is taken by the appellant and for the first time, this ground is raised before the Court.
Then coming to the valid driving license, admittedly, no ground is taken and this being a legal ground, this Court is inclined to consider the same.

In the light of the law laid down in National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Swaran Singh And Others 1, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

i. The Insurance Company shall pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

ii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy (
200 4) 3 SC C 297 NC: 2025:KHC:15035 of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iii. No costs.
iv. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
